title: Average US 401(k) Balance Hits Record High in Q2 2026
seoTitle: Average US 401(k) Balance Hits Record High in Q2 2026
subtitle: Fidelity Data Shows 10.5% Increase from Previous Quarter
excerpt: The average 401(k) balance in the United States reached $155,800 in Q2 2026, a historic record according to a Fidelity report, driven by...
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The average 401(k) balance in the United States reached $155,800 in the second quarter of 2026, setting a new record. The 10.5% increase from the previous quarter and 13.1% increase from the same period last year was reported in Fidelity Investments' "Building Financial Futures" report.

What the Record Average Balance Indicates

Fidelity's report indicates that the recovery of average 401(k) and 403(b) balances after a slight dip in the first quarter of 2026 led to the record level in the second quarter.

Factors Driving Growth

According to Jade Warshaw, co-host of "The Ramsey Show," the growth reflects years of strong market performance, increased participation from younger workers, and a growing desire for financial security amidst economic uncertainty.

Profile of More Active Investors

Warshaw notes that Generation Z has been investing more, motivated by a need for control over personal finances in an anxious economic landscape.

Recommendations for Those with High Balances

While increasing balances are positive, Warshaw warns against prioritizing retirement investments before establishing a solid financial foundation. She recommends following Ramsey Solutions' "7 Baby Steps," starting with a $1,000 emergency fund, paying off consumer debt, and setting aside three to six months of expenses.

Suggested Investment Strategy

To avoid market timing errors, Warshaw suggests investing in a "boring" way – that is, through regular contributions via payroll deductions, using the dollar-cost averaging technique. She compares this approach to "the tortoise and the hare," emphasizing that consistency offers a greater chance to accumulate long-term wealth.

With information from Fox Business.
